name: HOGAN, the Hon. Kevin John

headline.note: Hogan's finance, school, superannuation, small-business and farm work is documented, but hours, full-time status, exact boundaries and several employing entities remain unresolved. A school leadership title does not prove full-time work. Study, party activity, community roles and elected office are excluded; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Hogan's current biography identifies an economics degree; secondary material identifies Flinders University and completion in 1984. Start date, study load and employment overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: State Bank of NSW and Colonial State Bank (official wording; entity sequence unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official extract gives these employers, role and year boundaries. Current and secondary biographies describe Sydney finance work, a multi-billion-dollar portfolio and variants including GIO Securities and Colonial First State. Exact employer transitions, ownership/control at each date, appointment dates, hours and leave are unresolved; the entity variants are not silently collapsed into a precise chronology.
career_spells.counting_note: Finance employment is supported, but government control changed or is disputed across the named entities, and full-time status and exact boundaries are unproved.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary material identifies the qualification and 1998 completion; a published interview says Hogan completed a Diploma of Education before teaching. Enrolment dates, load and overlap with finance work are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Business Studies and Commerce teacher; Deputy Principal for an unresolved period
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official extract supplies the school and year boundaries. Hogan's and the Nationals' biographies identify teaching Business Studies and a period as Deputy Principal; an interview also identifies economics teaching. Exact appointment, leadership and departure dates, employing Catholic-school entity, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private/non-government school employment is supported, but substantive full-time status and exact dates are not established.

career_spells.employer: Catholic Superannuation and Retirement Fund (CSRF Industry Superannuation Fund)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen record gives Investment Officer from 2006 to 2008. Biographical and interview material says Hogan first served as a director through his teaching connections and later ran investments, travelling regularly to Sydney. Director dates, role transition, employment contract, exact boundaries, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private superannuation employment is supported, but governance and employment roles overlap unclearly and full-time status is not established.

career_spells.evidence_note: Current political biographies say Hogan operated a small business; secondary material calls it a consultancy after his superannuation work. Legal name, services, commencement, cessation, remuneration, hours and overlap with farming and campaigning are unresolved. The 2013 election is only an outer boundary, not proof of exact cessation.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is supported, but no countable full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Hogan family cattle property near Lismore
career_spells.evidence_note: Biographies say Hogan runs or ran his own farm/cattle property near Lismore; an interview places the property purchase on the move to the region in 1998. Ownership, business entity, active-work dates, hours, income, leave and continuation after election are unresolved; property ownership alone is not treated as continuous full-time work.
career_spells.counting_note: Private farming activity is supported, but hours and active-work boundaries are insufficient for calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: A published interview records joining the Nationals in 2009; secondary material records candidacy in 2010 and 2013. Membership, candidate remuneration, hours and overlaps with business/farm work are unresolved and party activity is not assumed to be employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and biographies establish House service from the 7 September 2013 election. Parliamentary, ministerial, shadow and party-room offices are nested within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

sources.title: Frozen official occupation/service extract
sources.note: Frozen record supplies finance, school and superannuation year ranges and House commencement; no roster refresh.

sources.title: About Kevin
sources.note: First-party biography identifies economics study, finance, Investment Officer work, teaching and Deputy Principal duties, small business and farming.

sources.title: The Hon. Kevin Hogan MP
sources.note: Party biography corroborates Colonial finance, teaching subjects and Deputy Principal duty, small business and cattle-property work.

sources.title: Kevin Hogan | Politician
sources.note: Interview supports the 1998 regional move/property purchase, education diploma, teaching subjects, CSRF director-to-investment transition and 2009 party membership.

sources.title: Kevin Hogan (politician)
sources.note: Secondary synthesis supplies education/employer variants, consultancy wording, cattle-property context and candidacy sequence; several career claims are marked citation-needed and retained as follow-up targets.

research_notes: Employer names in official and narrative biographies conflict for the 1989–1998 finance career; the record preserves that ambiguity rather than assigning years to unsupported entities.
The St Mary's role, omitted from the frozen occupation title, is identified as teaching and temporary Deputy Principal work by Hogan's current biography.
CSRF governance and paid investment work are not assumed to have identical dates or hours.
Farm ownership is not converted to continuous employment, and no post-election cessation is invented for business or farm activity.
open_questions: Which finance legal entities employed Hogan from 1989 to 1998, on what exact dates and under what government control at each transition?
Were the finance roles full-time, and what leave or breaks occurred?
What were the exact St Mary's appointment, Deputy Principal and departure dates, payroll entity, hours and leave?
What were the separate CSRF board and Investment Officer dates, remuneration, hours and employment status?
What was the consultancy/small-business legal entity, service, dates, income and weekly hours?
What active farm work and hours occurred before and after election, separately from property ownership?
Were the 2010 and 2013 federal candidacies remunerated or accompanied by other paid work?
